   - Background

   - Integrating SCI for Web ([@mrchrisadams](https://github.com/mrchrisadams))

     - The scope and targets of SCI for Web

   - Note: Keeping the meeting internal

   - SCI is primarily focused on carbon

   - SCI for web is focussed on web browsers

   - There is [SCI for AI](https://greensoftware.foundation/standards/sci-ai/) - oversubscribed

   - [SCI for Otel ](https://greensoftware.foundation/assemblies/sci-for-open-telemetry/)(open telemetry)

   - What is different?

     - Rather than using standards to design something, using standards to extract what is there. Pushing for vendor support quite early

     - SCI has the notion of a functional unit. We needed something repeatable. 

     - More detailed model than SCI

       - Client side

       - Vendor 

     - Tiered approach, allowing progressive detail where will and resources exit.

     - Various groups involved

     - Similar to https\://sustainablewebdesign.org

   - Presented as a segmented model for carbon emissions

   - Data transfer in there, but standard budges folks away from it.

   - We have the option to include the carbon footprint of the development process - CI, [GenAI](https://greensoftware.foundation/assemblies/), etc. We have left this as an option because it was too early.

   - Questions and comments:

     - We also include third parties because they contribute a great deal sustainability wise. 

     - With WSG-IR, we have quantitative and qualitative Success Criteria. We don’t know which ones are fully testable as we are not able to do any analytics. We know that some are going to be more difficult than others. 

     - Potential to use some kind of tooling - spread analysis of websites - what kind of impact it can have to come up with a better impact model.

     - Interested in the concept of functional units. Playwright has an amazing capacity to use resources. We need a minimal resource tool when it comes to functional units. Interested to use playwright to get a functional unit and include it in impact report in a more quantitative way. When I use it my laptop stops working…

       - Not aware of using the footprint of using playwright than something else. Closer to how humans use browsers. 

       - Can provide guidance to use efficient tools

     - Is there something leaner?

       - We can list alternatives

     - Question about using such tools which also add to unsustainability - transfer, processing and storage. One recommendation is to use smaller amounts of data and work on it.

     - The annoying part is about third parties - not knowing exact things to add into the equation. Is it in the plan to incorporate that?

       - Big spec has the whole thing about geo location and carbon intensity.

       - Averages that penalise the lack of disclosure

         - If something is below average then you need to share the details of this.

     - Light weight spec has specific language about reporting

     - What is the timeline?

       - The goal was to have everything finished and submitted to ISO by Q4. Plan is to submit by summer 2027

     - Having conversations with vendors, could you be able to build this. Have got comments from Adam. There is a paper on SCI for the web. Cardamom is a software that anyone can use 

       - <https://cardamon.io/>

     - Why ISO?

       - Makes things less risky. Some governments, such as India, Korea, will point to ISO but not W3C, etc

     - Relationship with SCI - ISO 21031

       - It is so flexible that it is hard to use.

       - If we want people to adopt it we need more detailed specs.

     - The Taiwan govt has not referred to WSG. We have not referred to ISO standards. We would love to standardize it under the W3C umbrella. 

       - The SCI for Web should be compatible with SCI. If a subset of the WSGIRs can be quantified in a way that is compatible with the SCI for Web, you could use / borrow the ISO status of the existing SCI. You could request metrics on the WSG-IRs that can have metrics reported. This would allow you to write it into a commercial agreement with vendors.

     - If we can get it to a point where we have the ability to have a system in place where people can go and know that this is something measurable. People can use it as part of showing evidence with ISO spec, which can be part of evidence. 

     - Is there a scope to incorporate this into ESG?

   - How does this incorporate in the impact ratings of WSG

     - When we were working on Impact Ratings we considered this. SCI for the web only looks at the carbon intensity and thus doesn’t incorporate the entire WSG. We can provide a nuisance way of balancing.

     - We have six pieces of the score, and this would be only one aspect of the score. Hope to bring it into impact rating, a neutral score that just doesn't come from our opinion but as a system. 

       - The current shape of the SCI web doesn't recognize stuff such as Google is making more convincing clean energy purchases than Amazon. This is problematic because we are adopting the existing framework of SCI.

     - If a data center is using energy from Iceland or shifting based on time of day, where does that show up in the guidelines? How does that affect their scoring?

       - It would primarily affect the planetary aspect of the scoring. The main area we would be adjusting the model - people, planet and prosperity - equivalent to ESG. 

     - There is a schema which should give you an idea. You could extend beyond that spec whatever green energy purchases you have. It only looks at the location based figures.

       - The SCI web is explicit about the carbon intensity of the electricity used to generate a score. So this means you can work backwards to get an idea of the electricity used.

       - If you wanted to recognise the use of clean energy, you could plausibly extend the SCI web spec with a market _based_ carbon intensity figure to accompany the _location based_ carbon intensity figure. This would be visible to people wanting to consume _SCI for Web_ scores, and pull out the two carbon intensity numbers.

     - We can say this is how we came to that score - basically provide evidence. We don’t necessarily lose anything. We can provide additional details (document) supporting stuff.

     - Real life scenario - Parents have solar panels generating 100% energy. Not a single tool was there to tell my carbon intensity. So this 100% claim didn’t mean anything - eg using raspberry pi on solar panels. So even if a tool says that we are using clean energy it would be difficult to prove whether this is the case.

       - On the GSF website, there is a teenager in France who reported something. 

       - There is a schema that you can use

     - What are we doing with the document and what folks want to know/do with SCI?

       - Two proposals heard

         - SCI for web for planetary scoring

         - Subset of WSG-IRs  - to provide a quantitative basis for some of the IRs.

     - GSF is working on water

       - Hybridised version - including SCI for web as part of measurement data

         - This is public too

         - <https://swi-guide.greensoftware.foundation/FormulaWalkthrough>

     - Carbon is a well understood problem. The mitigation of carbon emissions is a proxy for water and energy. Using less of it is good. So the beginning of measuring carbon is good.

     - Big drivers - energy consumption

     - This is an extremely complex topic - and would take years - what would make sense to actually find small pieces where we can put numbers and which can be standardized and is stable - and build on top of that…

       - E.g Are bytes a good proxy or not. As of now they are good to start with.

     - List of things Chris needs help with

       - Outside of TPAC, in one of the future meetings - provide structured precise feedback on this.

   - **Resolution**: We are going to use SCI for the planetary value  WSG-IR. Chris has a request for support.

     - 1 Neutral

     - 0 Opposition

     - Rest - Yes
